tagline:
Archive your dream today.
Break it into steps you can do.
spoken: [hook] You don't need a perfect resume. You need one clear sentence. || When someone asks what you do, most people say a job title, and then they ramble. Marketing, I guess, a bit of everything, it kind of depends. The other person nods, and forgets it by lunch. || [turn] So write one sentence with three parts. Who you help, what you help them do, and your proof. || For example. I help local cafés fill their quiet weekday hours, proven by a loyalty card that brought one café thirty new regulars. || Or for a developer. I help small clinics cut missed appointments with text reminders, proven by the system I built for my dentist. || Then put it everywhere. Your profile headline, the top of your resume, and the first line of every message you send. || Here's the test. Read it to a friend, and ask them to say it back. If they can't repeat it, cut words until they can. || [land] Write yours right now, in under twenty five words. Who you help, what you do, and your proof. || [outro] That's what Dmyor is for. You archive your dream today, so you can see it tomorrow, and break it down into small steps you can actually do. || [outro] If you want to try it out, I've put the link in the bio.
